question: Determine the number of solutions of $(k-1)x+2y=3$ and $2(k-1)x+4y=6$ for all real values of $k$. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Relationship between the equations
Multiplying the first equation by $2$ gives $$2(k-1)x+4y=6$$ which is exactly the second equation.
Dependence on the parameter
This relationship is valid for every real value of $k$, including $k=1$. When $k=1$, both equations reduce to equivalent equations in $y$.
Interpretation
The system contains only one independent linear equation in two variables. Every ordered pair satisfying the first equation also satisfies the second.
Number of solutions
Therefore, the system has infinitely many solutions for every $$k\in\mathbb{R}$$

options.A: The system has infinitely many solutions for every $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
options.B: The system has a unique solution for every $k\ne1$ and infinitely many solutions for $k=1$.
options.C: The system has no solution for $k=1$ and a unique solution otherwise.
options.D: The system has no solution for every $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
